Owner found the actual root cause after this session's multi-hour, multi-revert debugging saga: an INNER_SHADOW (or any) effect on a frame with NO FILL corrupts Figma's own text rendering for that frame's descendants -- specifically observed with Plus Jakarta Sans as a variable font (fontName.variationSettings, a weight-axis instance). This was Row's own divider implementation the whole time -- an INNER_SHADOW 'flood a 1px line at the bottom' effect on Row's own frame, which has no fill by design (rows in a recessed scroll track stay transparent). Every one of this session's three prior theories (text-style redefinition, instance-level text overrides, 'any sustained document activity') were each individually disproven by isolated testing -- all were red herrings; the real constant across every corrupted repro was simply 'an effect exists on this no-fill frame', which held in literal every attempt including the ones with zero text-style or instance touches, because the corrupting effect lived on the MASTER, inherited by every instance regardless of what else was or wasn't touched in a given attempt.
Fixed by replacing the effect with a real per-side stroke: strokeBottomWeight=1, strokeTopWeight/strokeLeftWeight/strokeRightWeight=0, strokeAlign='INSIDE', strokesIncludedInLayout=false (Card's own established inset-stroke technique, reused). Applied to the 12 non-focus variants (default+hover); the 6 focus variants keep their existing all-sides ring untouched, since it already visually covers the bottom edge with a more prominent color -- no conflict, no need for a second stroke layer. Verified via read-back: all 18 variants confirmed zero effects, correct stroke weights, focus ring intact where expected. Verified via export: text renders perfectly, zero corruption, across the full ListCard with all 9 live fleet rows (confirmed inherited the fix automatically, zero per-instance changes needed).
This attempt also redid the slot rename (plain 'status'/'action', no '(convert to Slot)' suffix) in the same pass -- both fixes landed clean together with no interaction (renaming layers has nothing to do with effects/fills, confirmed by this being the Nth time renaming alone was tested in isolation without ever corrupting anything).

General lesson for this file going forward, not just Row: never put an effect (shadow of any kind) directly on a frame that has no fill.
